subjects.displayTitle: Spiritual search: keeping desire and discernment alive
subjects.introduction: The fountain of divine generosity is gushing, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, but only the thirsty will drink from it, and the thirsty one must run after the water, for the fountain does not run after anyone. The steed of the valley of search, Bahá’u’lláh writes, is patience; the seeker should not falter if he strives a hundred thousand years without beholding the Friend, and he must set aside both the love and the hatred of any people lest the one keep him from investigating and the other from seeing truth where it stands. Truth is to be embraced in whatever lamp it shines, as a moth loves light, and when the lamp of longing is kindled the seeker finds himself with a new eye, a new ear, a new heart. Jesus’ invitation to ask, seek and knock sits in Luke between a neighbour’s persistent plea for bread and the Father’s readiness to give [1]. The road runs on through independent investigation of truth, through effort and striving, and along the spiritual path itself.
subjects.arc: Awaken thirst, cultivate fair-mindedness and patience, and follow inquiry into practice and renewed perception.

order.why: Establish patience and inquiry rather than imitation.
shortened: The steed of this valley is patience; without patience the wayfarer on this journey will reach nowhere and attain no goal. Nor should he ever become downhearted: If he strive for a hundred thousand years and yet fail to behold the beauty of the Friend, he should not falter. For those who seek the Kaaba of "for Us" rejoice in the tidings "In Our ways shall We assuredly guide them."
O My brother, consider these matters in the spirit of enquiry, not in blind imitation.

order.why: Open with the need for thirst at an abundant fountain.
shortened: The fountain of divine generosity is gushing forth, but we must have thirst for the living waters. Unless there be thirst, the salutary water will not assuage.

order.why: Hear the reported insistence that the seeker must move.
Distinguish degrees of entering the garden.
Consider fairness and freedom from obstructing loves and hatreds.
shortened: First, he must be fair-minded and detached from all save God. His heart must be entirely directed towards the Supreme Horizon and freed from the bondage of vain and selfish desires, for these are obstacles on the path. Furthermore, he must endure every tribulation, embody the utmost purity and sanctity, and renounce the love or hatred of all the peoples of the world, lest his love for one thing hinder him from investigating another, or his hatred for something prevent him from discerning its truth.

order.why: Read the discipline of seeing things in their proper stations.
shortened: Know thou of a truth that the seeker must, at the beginning of his quest for God, enter the Garden of Search. In this journey it behoveth the wayfarer to detach himself from all save God and to close his eyes to all that is in the heavens and on the earth. There must not linger in his heart either the hate or the love of any soul, to the extent that they would hinder him from attaining the habitation of the celestial Beauty.

It behoveth thine eminence in this station to consider each created thing in its own place, neither abasing nor exalting its true rank. For instance, if thou wert to reduce the unseen world to the realm of creation, this would be an act of sheer blasphemy, and the converse would likewise be the essence of impiety. Wert thou, however, to describe the unseen world and the realm of creation within their own stations, this would be the undoubted truth.
Comprehend, in like manner, every station, sign, and allusion, that thou mayest perceive all things in their own place and consider all matters in their proper light.

order.why: Seek light beyond attachment to a particular lamp.
Explore the lamp of search and the transformation of perception.
shortened: Only when the lamp of search, of earnest striving, of longing desire, of passionate devotion, of fervid love, of rapture, and ecstasy, is kindled within the seeker's heart, and the breeze of His loving-kindness is wafted upon his soul, will the darkness of error be dispelled, the mists of doubts and misgivings be dissipated, and the lights of knowledge and certitude envelop his being. At that hour will the mystic Herald, bearing the joyful tidings of the Spirit, shine forth from the City of God resplendent as the morn, and, through the trumpet-blast of knowledge, will awaken the heart, the soul, and the spirit from the slumber of negligence. Then will the manifold favors and outpouring grace of the holy and everlasting Spirit confer such new life upon the seeker that he will find himself endowed with a new eye, a new ear, a new heart, and a new mind.

order.why: Enter the ocean of words through active study.
shortened: Immerse yourselves in the ocean of My words, that ye may unravel its secrets, and discover all the pearls of wisdom that lie hid in its depths. Take heed that ye do not vacillate in your determination to embrace the truth of this Cause--a Cause through which the potentialities of the might of God have been revealed, and His sovereignty established.

order.why: Hear the reported call to discover every truth.
Include sciences and arts in strenuous learning.
shortened: Ye must therefore put forth a mighty effort, striving by night and day and resting not for a moment, to acquire an abundant share of all the sciences and arts, that the Divine Image, which shineth out from the Sun of Truth, may illumine the mirror of the hearts of men.

order.why: Read the reported counsel on study, prayer and living the life.
Consider hunger as preparation for a spiritual table.
Read the reported invitation to remain thirsty.
Hear the call to kindle an ardent search.
Follow the birds, flower and consuming flame of love.
shortened: In the Rose Garden of changeless splendor a Flower hath begun to bloom, compared to which every other flower is but a thorn, and before the brightness of Whose glory the very essence of beauty must pale and wither. Arise, therefore, and, with the whole enthusiasm of your hearts, with all the eagerness of your souls, the full fervor of your will, and the concentrated efforts of your entire being, strive to attain the paradise of His presence, and endeavor to inhale the fragrance of the incorruptible Flower, to breathe the sweet savors of holiness, and to obtain a portion of this perfume of celestial glory.

Whoso followeth this counsel will break his chains asunder, will taste the abandonment of enraptured love, will attain unto his heart's desire, and will surrender his soul into the hands of his Beloved. Bursting through his cage, he will, even as the bird of the spirit, wing his flight to his holy and everlasting nest.

order.why: Consider becoming a light through longing and effort.
shortened: Only the one who is willing to become like an adoring moth around the flame shall shine even as a lighted candle. Such a one must strive by day and night, must cry aloud and beg to behold the rays of truth shining from the Dawning Place of all lights.

order.why: Hear longing recognized in prayer.
Widen the prayer for seeking to the world.
Connect progress with exertion.
Read expenditure beside the need for sustaining income.
shortened: O ye friends, exert ye an effort! Every expenditure is in need of an income.

order.why: Consider the reported effort required for detachment.
shortened: We must strive to attain to that condition by being separated from all the things and people of the world, and seeing God only. It will take some effort and trouble on our part to attain to this condition; we must work for it, strive for it.

order.why: Describes the detachment and purity required of a seeker.
Read sovereignty as mastery of self and passion.
Join recognition with observance.
shortened: Say: O ye lovers of the One true God! Strive, that ye may truly recognize and know Him, and observe befittingly His precepts.

order.why: Consider a daily movement toward the threshold of oneness.
shortened: Consequently, rest ye not, seek ye no composure, attach not yourselves to the luxuries of this ephemeral world, free yourselves from every attachment, and strive with heart and soul to become fully established in the Kingdom of God. Gain ye the heavenly treasures. Day by day become ye more illumined. Draw ye nearer and nearer unto the threshold of oneness.

order.why: Read earnest labor in the setting of sacrifice.
shortened: Now is the time, O ye beloved of the Lord, for ardent endeavour. Struggle ye, and strive. And since the Ancient Beauty was exposed by day and night on the field of martyrdom, let us in our turn labour hard, and hear and ponder the counsels of God; let us fling away our lives, and renounce our brief and numbered days.

order.why: Seek courage and spiritual power.
shortened: Tell the maidservant of God Kerry Kinney and Percy Grant to increase their attention to the Kingdom as much as they can so they may find innate courage and seek spiritual power.

order.why: Consider search that scholarly standing cannot replace.
shortened: O seekers of truth! The struggle and search for truth is a heavy burden, and the trust of the Glorious Lord is such that heaven and earth cannot bear it. Therefore, the learned and accomplished who did not seek became deprived. But since you were seekers of truth, you strived and struggled, became privy to the mystery and became intimate confidants with the Beloved of mysteries.

order.why: Ask what makes hearing receptive.
Read the frozen heart and deficient perception as spiritual images.
Acknowledge the beginning of a particular seeker’s inquiry.
Find guidance within images of desert, water and light.
shortened: If you are lost in the desert, the path of guidance is clear and evident. If you thirst for the sweet Euphrates, the waves of the creative sea are high and manifest. And if you long for the divine countenance, the lights of His presence from the Most Glorious Kingdom are clear and visible to the eye of insight.

order.why: Hear the reported assurance of a teacher for the earnest seeker.
Read the promise that sincere seeking is received.
Hear the accompanying assurance of access.
Consider gratitude for a quest that has borne fruit.
Read the path traced toward the Traceless Friend.
Close the linked sequence by sharing what the ocean gives.
shortened: O thou who journeyest unto God! Take thy portion from this ocean and deprive not thyself of that which hath been ordained therein, and be of them that attain. Were all who are in the heavens and earth to be given but a drop thereof, they would find themselves enriched through the enrichment of God, the Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Take, with the hand of detachment, a handful from this Living Ocean, then sprinkle it upon all created things, that they may be purified from human limitations and be brought nigh unto the Most Sublime Vision of God, this hallowed and resplendent spot.

order.why: Retain the supplied invitation to seek pearls through effort.
Read the supplied statement connecting spiritual life with seeking.
Hear the supplied Christian mystical voice on active love.
Retain Luke’s supplied invitation to ask and seek.
Close with supplied encouragement for ordinary believers who prepare and serve.

questions: What awakens a desire for truth, and what can gradually dull it?
How might love and aversion each interfere with fair-minded inquiry?
What would patience look like without becoming passivity or unquestioning acceptance?
Which practices in the compilation connect searching with changes in conduct?
How does Luke’s setting of need and generosity affect your understanding of asking and receiving?
What could it mean to find something valuable while remaining open to further discovery?

references.label: 1 · Luke 11:5–13 · Asking, seeking and receiving
references.note: Read the supplied invitation to seek within its larger Gospel setting: a visitor needing bread, persistent asking, and the Father’s gift of the Holy Spirit. Compare initiative and trust with the collection’s thirst and patience. The passage concerns prayer and divine generosity; it does not promise that every preference or preconception will be confirmed.

subjects.displayTitle: Justice and mercy: protecting rights, opening a future
subjects.introduction: A labourer who has worked from morning till evening is owed his wage; that is justice. To reward him when he has done nothing is bounty. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s homely example opens a subject that soon becomes demanding, because the two responses to human need pull in different directions and a life needs both. If someone wrongs you personally, you are to forgive; if they wrong everyone, their victims’ rights are not yours to give away, and the social body must rise to protect. No one may take vengeance, yet reward and punishment remain the two pillars of world order. Kindness shown to the tyrant or the thief only confirms them in their ways, while a government that saves predators from their own nature consoles the oppressed. Rulers and judges who remember that they will reap what they sow find their judgments growing just. Micah folds the whole matter into one summons, to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with God [1], and humility is the right ending, since whoever prays for bounty rather than strict deserts learns how to extend it. From here the path leads to forgiveness and grace, to social and divine justice, and to reward and punishment.
subjects.arc: Distinguish what is owed from what is given, examine protection without revenge, and return to grace and humility.

order.why: Keep the reported account of justice as giving each their due.
shortened: The justice and mercy of God is very difficult a subject and requires much reflection upon our Lord's words. First to know the meaning of justice. It is not equality, but the giving to everyone according to his right. But it isn't that one deals with a learned man in the same way with an enemy and friend is not Justice, nor to deal with animal and man in the same way. The meaning of Justice is to give what is due to each one--to deal differently with the learned and ignorant.

order.why: Open with wages, gifts and forgiveness as distinct examples.
shortened: Know that justice consists in rendering to each his due. For example, when a workman labours from morning till evening, justice requires that he be paid his wage, but bounty consists in rewarding him even when he has done no work and expended no effort. So when you give alms to a poor man who has made no effort and done nothing for your benefit to deserve it, this is bounty. Thus, Christ besought forgiveness for those responsible for His death: This is called bounty.

order.why: Read guidance as gift beyond merit.
shortened: O sign of bounty! The favors of the Sovereign of existence which are given according to merit - which means giving each rightful one their due - fall under the requirements of justice. However, the Most Great Guidance is a supreme gift and pertains to grace and bounty.

order.why: Hear the petition for bounty beyond strict deserts.
shortened: Do not look to lack of capacity, but consider bounty alone as the measure. Beseech His Holiness the One God for grace, that He may open the gate of bounty and not decree justice. For justice is giving each their due right, and if matters proceeded thus it would become difficult and complicated.

order.why: Read the related reported formulation without erasing its difference.
Distinguish obedience from the receipt of grace.
Consider the difference between one’s own grievance and others’ rights.
shortened: If someone transgresses against you personally, you should forgive them. But if they transgress against everyone, you cannot forgive everyone's right. Therefore the social body must rise up to defend and protect.

order.why: Hear the reported counsel against personal retaliation.
Hold the rejection of vengeance beside public accountability.
Read a specific prohibition on taking retribution personally.
Consider protection of the oppressed with the express rejection of revenge.
shortened: But consider the future: if a just government arises as it should to establish justice and equity, saving the predators from their predatory nature and consoling the oppressed, it will become the cause of success and prosperity and be confirmed in salvation and deliverance. We do not seek revenge nor are we content with anyone's punishment and torment. However, if severe retribution is not enacted, wolves will continually test their claws in the blood of God's sheep and will not rest for a moment except to stain their teeth and claws with pure blood.

order.why: Examine kindness that enables continued wrongdoing.
Read mercy directed toward transformation of an aggressor.
shortened: Let the friends of God be the source of moderation and restraint, therefore; let them be the source of mercy and generosity to others. My hope is that they may illumine this dark world and show kindness to all its peoples, that they will treat the stranger as a friend and the deprived one as an intimate companion, that they will be compassionate towards the ignorant and offer guidance to the aggressor in such wise he may acquire angelic qualities, be free from violence, transform these instincts of cruelty to those of trust, adopt the characteristics of the meek and accept the way of these exiles.

order.why: Distinguish justice from the execution of selfish desire.
Distinguishes mercy from strict justice in considering those compelled to fight in war.
Keep the argument about indiscriminate amnesty in its context.
Read the reported claim concerning crime and collective welfare.
shortened: If a person commit a crime against you, you have not the right to forgive him; but the law must punish him in order to prevent a repetition of that same crime by others, as the pain of the individual is unimportant beside the general welfare of the people.

order.why: Question inherited guilt through the example of father and son.
shortened: Could we conceive of the Divinity, Who is Justice itself, inflicting punishment upon the posterity of Adam for Adam's own sin and disobedience? Even if we should see a governor, an earthly ruler punishing a son for the wrongdoing of his father, we would look upon that ruler as an unjust man. Granted the father committed a wrong, what was the wrong committed by the son? There is no connection between the two.

order.why: Hold hope of forgiveness beside responsibility for conduct.
Consider the educational analogy in its historical wording.
shortened: A father or a teacher sometimes rewards children and sometimes punishes them. The purpose of his punishment is to train his children and is actually a form of mercy and kindness unto them. Although it appears as wrath yet in reality it is compassion. If it appears on the surface to involve hurt and pain inwardly it is sweet and refreshing water.

order.why: Connect institutions with changing needs and problems.
Read justice and wisdom as supports of tranquility.
Consider the responsibility attributed to public officials.
Read the reported ruler’s choice between fairness and tyranny.
Hear the reported aspiration to equal justice for rich and poor.
Retain the particular reported assessment of law in its setting.
Include the reported account of education and social welfare.
Consider due rights alongside distinctions of capacity and recompense.
Apply the demand for justice to professional power.
Read mercy and fairness in the concrete matter of peasants’ property.
shortened: As to what thou didst write regarding the property at the door of the house which is with the peasants, that whatever they have should be taken, whether livestock or other things that may exist - after this matter was presented He said: "O Ali, fix thy gaze upon the horizon of justice and fairness. Action must not depart from mercy and loving-kindness.

order.why: Consider the image of government as shepherd.
Hear the hope that great and humble find ease.
shortened: May God grant success. We hope that soon a just government will be established and both great and humble will find comfort and ease.

order.why: Connect justice with oneness and fellowship.
Keep the specific distinction between government and troublemakers.
shortened: The government itself, praise be to God, is just and generous, but the troublemakers do not rest and commit oppression against the faithful ones.

order.why: Retain the particular hope concerning a new government.
Read another historically situated judgment about recompense.
shortened: Praise be to God that the secret instigator of this affair has received the recompense for his deeds, and it is hoped that a just government will arise to deal with equity and fairness and become a manifestation of the All-Merciful, the Compassionate.

order.why: Keep the reported criticism of rulers’ whims.
Read the reported statement on forfeited authority in its particular source.
Keep the wartime interpretation as a reported historical claim.
Read the peace-making invitation spoken by the king in the Alexander story.
shortened: Let us be friends and comrades and not as warring enemies. I invite you and all your army to be my guests for a few months. We will spread the feasts of joy and merry making and consort with each other with perfect intimacy. Our men instead of killing each other will live side by side. Is not this better than the grim battlefield strewn with dead and wounded?"

order.why: Consider the reported balance weighed by mercy and fellowship.
shortened: As to the fifth verse: When all these brutalities are committed, when governments and nations have had enough carnage, bloodshed, destruction, then the Balances of Divine Justice will be set up. Those souls who have been kind and merciful, who have promoted peace and good-fellowship, who have joined the rank of the army of the Kingdom or in other words those "whose balances are heavy" that is; his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds - he shall attain to the good-pleasure of the Lord and receive not only the approbation of all mankind but of his Creator who watches over all things and who loveth a faithful steward.

order.why: Hear the lament over justice obscured by greed.
shortened: Justice and fairness have vanished from the world and the oppressors of the age are ablaze with the fire of greed and passion.

order.why: Read the prayer from amid oppression.
Consider prayer for a ruler’s illumination.
shortened: Until now His Majesty the King hath not become aware of the good intent of this Wronged One, though the people of God are well aware of it. This Wronged One hath, in most of His Tablets, made mention of His Majesty and hath beseeched from God--glorified be His mention--justice for him and sought fairness on his behalf. We beseech the Most High at this moment to illumine him with the light of justice which shall endure as long as the Kingdom of God, the Mighty, the Wondrous, shall endure.

order.why: Hear another petition for justice and restraint of oppression.
Turn toward walking in the ways of justice.
shortened: Arise to help the Cause of God, then walk in the ways of justice and shun the paths of the oppressors.

order.why: Read the concise counsel against transgression.
Connect protection with security and generosity.
Hear mercy described as preceding the exercise of wrath.
shortened: They are like unto mere children, and our Lord is the Educator of the world. If We but willed, we could have seized them with a single word from Us, yet the mercy of the Lord, the Almighty, the All-Glorious, the All-Powerful, supersedes His wrath.

order.why: Consider grace together with justice.
shortened: By God! He dealeth with grace after justice hath appeared through this straight Balance.

order.why: Read both attributes as encompassing the worlds.
shortened: Say: Contend not with anyone, nor deny any soul's rights. Consider ye the justice of God and His mercy which encompasseth the worlds.

order.why: Hear the petition for recompense and divine presence.
shortened: We beseech God, exalted be He, to reward them for their deeds in this world and the next and to decree for them the recompense of attaining His presence. Verily He is the Forgiving, the Generous.

order.why: Consider the difference between intimacy and trepidation.
shortened: When Thou bestowest favor there is intimacy, and when Thou showest justice there is trepidation. Thou art the Merciful, the Generous, and the Kind.

order.why: Close with a prayer for pardon beyond one’s deserts.
shortened: O my Lord, my Hope, the Ultimate Goal of my aspirations and the End of my desires! I beseech Thee by the sovereignty of Thy forgiveness which encompasses all created things, and by the vastness of the ocean of Thy pardon wherein are immersed all sinners among contingent beings, and by the outpourings of Thy clemency which have flooded all creation, to enfold this servant in the beauty of Thy pardon, to strengthen him with the hosts of Thy forgiveness, to treat him according to Thy grace and not according to Thy justice, and to fulfill Thy promise regarding Thy servant.

questions: What does the distinction between a wage and a gift clarify, and where does it leave questions open?
How can personal forgiveness coexist with the protection of people harmed by wrongdoing?
What could distinguish accountability aimed at transformation from revenge?
How do the passages concerning rulers and professionals connect power with responsibility?
What does Micah’s inclusion of humility add to the practice of justice and mercy?
Where might seeking mercy for oneself enlarge one’s capacity to act fairly toward others?

references.label: 1 · Micah 6:6–8 · Justice, mercy and humility
references.note: The prophet moves from questions about extravagant offerings to a summons concerning justice, mercy, and humility before God. Compare this joined ethical demand with the compilation’s distinctions between rights, public protection, personal forgiveness, and divine bounty. Micah’s concise summons is not a detailed theory of punishment, but can inform reflection on the spirit in which power is exercised.

subjects.introduction: Two people who promise to improve each other’s spiritual life have taken on an exacting and beautiful task. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes husband and wife as a single soul, two helpmates and intimate friends who should be concerned for each other’s welfare, consulting with the utmost love, keeping faith with one another, and letting their unity grow day by day until it becomes one spirit and one body. A bond that is only physical, he warns, is doomed to end in separation; a union of body and spirit is a gleam of the love of God and endures through all His worlds. Such a marriage asks for care in knowing another’s character before the covenant is made, for sacrifice freely offered rather than demanded, and for a home whose love flows outward into service. The Buddhist Samajivina Sutta, where a couple wishing to stay together are told to match each other in conviction, virtue, generosity and discernment, offers a kindred vision of shared cultivation while describing future life in its own distinct terms [1]. The verse of the Kitáb-i-Aqdas on marriage belongs with its published explanation that monogamy is enjoined [2]. From here the way opens toward the laws that frame marriage and its dowry, the prayers revealed for married couples, and the wider questions a family faces about children and their coming.
subjects.arc: Begin with mutual spiritual growth, develop the practices of companionship, and consider its enduring and wider purposes.

order.why: Open with character, commitment and the growth of both partners.
shortened: Each must, however, exercise the utmost care to become thoroughly acquainted with the character of the other, that the binding covenant between them may be a tie that will endure forever. Their purpose must be this: to become loving companions and comrades and at one with each other for time and eternity

The true marriage of Baha'is is this, that husband and wife should be united both physically and spiritually, that they may ever improve the spiritual life of each other, and may enjoy everlasting unity throughout all the worlds of God.

order.why: Read companionship as concern for each other’s welfare.
shortened: O ye two believers in God! The Lord, peerless is He, hath made woman and man to abide with each other in the closest companionship, and to be even as a single soul. They are two helpmates, two intimate friends, who should be concerned about the welfare of each other.
If they live thus, they will pass through this world with perfect contentment, bliss, and peace of heart, and become the object of divine grace and favour in the Kingdom of heaven.
Strive, then, to abide, heart and soul, with each other as two doves in the nest, for this is to be blessed in both worlds.

order.why: Make loving consultation practical.
Hear the reported insistence on freely given service without force.
shortened: A condition must be realized in which the man and woman sacrifice their right for each other, serve each other with heart and soul and not through force and violence. This condition cannot be realized except through the power of faith. Hearts must be attracted to the divine fragrances so that each one prefers the other to himself and does not consider himself above the other.

order.why: Consider reciprocal loyalty and the danger of jealousy.
shortened: The greatest bond that will unite the hearts of man and wife is faithfulness and loyalty. Both must exercise toward each other the utmost faithfulness and loyalty and not let any trace of jealousy creep between them; for this thing like unto poison vitiates the very foundation of love.

The man and wife must dedicate their knowledge, their talents, their fortunes, their titles, their bodies and their spirits, first to Baha'u'llah and then to each other. Their thoughts must be lofty, their ideals luminous, their hearts spiritual, and their souls the dawning-places of the rays of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Read the longstanding rights of companions.
shortened: In truth, one must arise in faithfulness and show firmness and steadfastness, especially to one's companion, associate, intimate friend and confidant, for the rights between these two are ancient, firm and strong.

order.why: Think of unity as something increasing day by day.
Ground affection in a spiritual relationship.
Connects affection between spouses with spiritual development.
Explore the relation of physical and spiritual union.
shortened: Marriage, among the mass of the people, is a physical bond, and this union can only be temporary, since it is foredoomed to a physical separation at the close.

Among the people of Baha, however, marriage must be a union of the body and of the spirit as well, for here both husband and wife are aglow with the same wine, both are enamoured of the same matchless Face, both live and move through the same spirit, both are illumined by the same glory. This connection between them is a spiritual one, hence it is a bond that will abide forever.

order.why: Read the reported account of a family’s spiritual atmosphere.
Keep the reported call to comfort and assist one another.
Consider the qualities sought in choosing a companion.
shortened: Marry thou a wise, perfect, learned, experienced and faithful person, so that thy time may pass in joy and happiness from beginning up to the end.

order.why: Read patience in a particular prospective relationship.
shortened: O Handmaid of God! Do not hurry the matter, as it is better to wait a while in such affairs. Perchance that person's heart may be illumined with the light of guidance, and thou mayest draw him nearer the shade of the Tree of Life and enable him to enter the paradise of divine love. Tell him: "I desire intimacy and union with thee in both the earthly and divine kingdoms, both physically and spiritually. Were we to be united in body only and remain distant in spirit, what use and benefit would such a union bring? For such intimacy would be a transitory thing and not an essential reality. Rather would I share a bond with thee in both the earthly and heavenly realms, in both body and spirit.

order.why: Retain the requirement of consent and the accompanying blessing.
Include consultation about a particular marriage.
Hear the reported emphasis on the bond’s importance.
shortened: He answered: "The marriage bond is very important." He repeated it again: "Very very important. Marriage must be strict and pure. You must all be very careful about this."

order.why: Consider the reported responsibilities of covenant.
Read marriage as a fortress for well-being.
shortened: And when He desired to manifest grace and beneficence to men, and to set the world in order, He revealed observances and created laws; among them He established the law of marriage, made it as a fortress for well-being and salvation, and enjoined it upon us in that which was sent down out of the heaven of sanctity in His Most Holy Book. He saith, great is His glory: "Enter into wedlock, O people, that ye may bring forth one who will make mention of Me amid My servants. This is My bidding unto you; hold fast to it as an assistance to yourselves."

order.why: Retain the Aqdas selection with the linked contextual note on monogamy.
Consider the covenant as a sign of unity.
Read the Word of God as a source of affinity.
shortened: The wife is a being who wishes to be overflowing with and seeks after the attributes of God and His names; and the tie between them is no other than the Word of God. Verily, it (the Word of God) causes the multitudes to assemble together, and the remote ones to be united. Thus the husband and wife are brought into affinity, are united and harmonized, even as though they were one person. Through their mutual union, companionship and love great results are produced in the world, both material and spiritual.

order.why: Follow companionship toward material and spiritual results.
shortened: Thus the husband and wife are brought into affinity, are united and harmonized, even as though they were one person. Through their mutual union, companionship and love great results are produced in the world, both material and spiritual.

order.why: Explore the broader image of union in creation.
shortened: From separation doth every kind of hurt and harm proceed, but the union of created things doth ever yield most laudable results. From the pairing of even the smallest particles in the world of being are the grace and bounty of God made manifest; and the higher the degree, the more momentous is the union.

And above all other unions is that between human beings, especially when it cometh to pass in the love of God. Thus is the primal oneness made to appear; thus is laid the foundation of love in the spirit.

order.why: Hear the blessing upon gladdened hearts.
Read the congratulations offered to a particular couple.
shortened: Now your engagement is the greatest expression of love and affection. It will certainly yield great results. You have formed a blessed family. The exalted Hosts will spread their congratulations over you and the inhabitants of the Kingdom of Abha will convey their felicitations.

order.why: Consider a marriage linking Iran and America.
Keep the counsel concerning distance of kinship in its source form.
Retain the historical reported claim about race and heredity as a reported claim.
Consider attachment that displaces the spiritual purpose of the bond.
Read the related warning concerning adoration of a partner.
Join marriage with continuing service.
shortened: Thou canst take unto thyself a husband and at the same time serve the Cause of God; the one doth not preclude the other.

order.why: Hear the brief reported praise of spiritual illumination.
Read the reported vision of joyful companionship and an ordered home.
shortened: It is highly important for man to raise a family. So long as he is young, because of youthful self-complacency, he does not realize its significance, but this will be a source of regret when he grows old...

In this glorious Cause the life of a married couple should resemble the life of the angels in heaven -- a life full of joy and spiritual delight, a life of unity and concord, a friendship both mental and physical. The home should be orderly and well-organized.

order.why: Keep the blessing offered to a couple forming a family.
Consider the reported perspective of later life.
Read the expansive spiritual purpose ascribed to wedlock.
shortened: When the rustling of the Divine Lote-Tree was raised, it called out saying: Praise be to God Who hath made marriage a portal for the manifestation of the dawning-places of His name, the All-Merciful, and through it have the cities of remembrance and utterance been adorned.
And praise be to God Who hath made wedlock a means for the promotion of His Cause among His servants and the proclamation of His Word throughout His lands.

order.why: Hear the hope for a fruitful shared life.
shortened: For the enlightenment of the world dependeth upon the existence of man. If man did not exist in this world, it would have been like a tree without fruit. My hope is that you both may become even as one tree, and may, through the outpourings of the cloud of loving-kindness, acquire freshness and charm, and may blossom and yield fruit, so that your line may eternally endure.

order.why: Consider character and the lasting influence of descendants.
shortened: O seeker after righteous deeds that endure!

Children and grandchildren who, being of noble lineage, are aided by goodly character - that is to say, who are illumined by the effulgences of the Luminary of the horizons - are to be counted among righteous deeds that endure.

order.why: Read the prayer’s image of two seas of love.
shortened: Wherefore, wed Thou in the heaven of Thy mercy these two birds of the nest of Thy love, and make them the means of attracting perpetual grace; that from the union of these two seas of love a wave of tenderness may surge and cast the pearls of pure and goodly issue on the shore of life.

order.why: Join the prayer for union with growth in spirituality and service.
Close the linked sequence with two birds singing together.
shortened: When two birds sing on the branches of a cedar with sweet melodies in remembrance of God those melodies will reach the highest summit from this nether region and it will exhilarate the denizens of the temples of the Kingdom.

order.why: Retain the supplied statement on the enduring command.
Close with the supplied distinction between spiritual friendship and predetermined soul mates.

questions: What does helping another person grow spiritually ask of one’s daily conduct?
How can consultation develop a shared purpose while giving both partners a full voice?
What distinguishes mutual sacrifice freely offered from pressure or coercion?
How do the images of one soul, two birds, and a fruitful tree illuminate different aspects of companionship?
What does the Buddhist couple’s shared practice reveal, and how does its account of future life differ?
How might an enduring friendship widen into service beyond the household?

references.label: 1 · Samajivina Sutta · Living in tune (AN 4.55)
references.note: In Thanissaro Bhikkhu’s translation, Nakula’s parents ask about remaining together in this life and the next. The response emphasizes harmony in conviction, virtue, generosity, and discernment. Compare shared cultivation and loving speech with the compilation’s concern for mutual spiritual growth, while preserving the distinct Buddhist account of future existence.

references.label: 2 · Contextual reading: Kitáb-i-Aqdas, note 89
references.note: This published note supplies the authorized interpretive context for the Aqdas passage included here. It explains ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that monogamy is enjoined and that the condition attached to taking a second wife cannot be fulfilled. Read the excerpt with this explanation rather than as an isolated permission.

subjects.displayTitle: Mind and nature: discovery, power and responsibility
subjects.introduction: A voice that should have faded with its vibrations is stored in a box; electricity, a force that can cleave mountains, is shut in a glass bulb and told to give light; a creature without wings or fins crosses the air and the sea. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá keeps pointing to such ordinary marvels and asks what they say about the one who made them. The sun cannot leave its orbit; every other creature is nature’s captive; but the human spirit discovers the hidden natures of things and, by that discovery, bends them to its purpose. Whether this is called breaking nature’s laws or using them, a power that stands above nature must come from somewhere nature does not reach. Bacon, who tied human power to patient observation of causes, described the method of such mastery without asking what kind of being is capable of it [1]. The Bahá’í writings ask exactly that, and then press the harder question of responsibility, since the same intellect can serve healing or harm. The way onward leads through the mind’s power of discovery, what distinguishes man from the animal, the two natures that contend in every soul, and the principle that the higher always encompasses the lower.
subjects.arc: Rediscover ordinary inventions, examine the language of mastery, and connect intellectual power with moral purpose.

order.why: Read explicitly how material laws are used to overcome limitations.
Open with the surprising preservation of a human voice.
Hear the reported extension of bodily capacities.
shortened: He has no wings, but he does not submit himself to this fact; he makes wings and conquers the air. He has no fins, but he conquers the sea. He conquers the night by creating for himself light; the cold by making heat; his limited senses by supplementing and extending them.

order.why: Connect mastery with discovery of the natures of things.
Survey the varied products of the mind.
Consider hidden possibilities becoming visible inventions.
shortened: All that you observe of crafts, wonders, effects and discoveries was once in the realm of the unseen and was a hidden matter. The human spirit discovered that hidden secret and brought it from the realm of the unseen to the world of being. For example, steam power, photography, phonography, telegraphy, mathematical problems - all of these were once hidden secrets and protected mysteries.

order.why: Read gradual discovery through human reality.
shortened: Know, therefore, that the human reality encompasses the realities of all things and discovers their true nature, their properties, and their mysteries. For instance, all the existing crafts, inventions, sciences, and branches of learning have been discovered by the human reality. At one time they were all hidden and concealed mysteries, but the reality of man gradually discovered them and brought them forth from the invisible world into the visible realm.

order.why: Connect discovery with the rational soul.
shortened: Through the power of the rational soul man can discover the realities of things, comprehend their properties and penetrate the mysteries of existence. All the sciences, branches of learning, arts, inventions, institutions, undertakings and discoveries have resulted from the comprehension of the rational soul. These were once impenetrable secrets, hidden mysteries and unknown realities, and the rational soul gradually discovered them and brought them out of the invisible plane into the realm of the visible.

order.why: Hear the emergence of new enterprises and inventions.
shortened: Thus, great discoveries have been made, mighty enterprises have been established, wonderful inventions have appeared, and the mysteries of the universe have stepped forth from the invisible plane into the realm of the visible.

order.why: Read the reported examples of technologies brought to light.
Consider the same movement from hidden to known.
Read the linked examples of light, sound and communication.
shortened: For instance, he imprisons in an incandescent lamp the illimitable natural energy called electricity -- a material force which can cleave mountains -- and bids it give him light. He takes the human voice and confines it in the phonograph for his benefit and amusement. According to his natural power man should be able to communicate a limited distance, but by overcoming the restrictions of nature he can annihilate space and send telephone messages thousands of miles.

order.why: Focus on electricity as illumination and communication.
Consider the transformation of a city at night.
Read aviation as an example of transcending bodily limits.
shortened: But the reasonable or intellectual reality with which man is endowed enables him to transcend the laws of physical nature. For example, according to the laws of nature man is a denizen of the earth; he must walk upon the earth, and, because he is born on this globe, he belongs to this earthly life. This is a regulation of nature. But man, through his intellectual power transcends this law of nature, discovers the science of aviation and flies in the air like a bird.

order.why: Place ships and flight beside the account of human distinction.
Enter the extended rhetoric of nature’s captivity and human invention.
shortened: Man, however, is the opposite - he is nature's master. For example, according to nature's requirements and laws, man is an earthbound creature, not one of air or water. Yet despite this natural law, he breaks nature's rule - he soars through the air, traverses the surface of the sea as if it were an open field, runs upon the waters, and pilots vessels beneath them. This contravenes nature's universal law.
Thus it is evident that man breaks nature's law and is therefore the noblest of all created things, for he possesses universal capabilities.

order.why: Consider the contrast between the sun and human agency.
Read another address’s statement of that contrast.
Keep the image of captured electricity in its reported setting.
Read the vivid sword image through the role of knowledge.
Hear the strongest rhetorical account of human power.
Consider the power attributed to the human spirit.
Read the reported examples of movement beyond customary limits.
shortened: Look and see how all beings cannot transgress beyond the world of nature - they are captive, but humans are free from nature's bondage for they break through nature. For example, observe that according to nature living things are earthbound, yet humans fly in the air - this is against nature. They move upon the sea and travel beneath it - this breaks the general law of nature.

order.why: Keep the reported sword and lamp images together.
Consider the challenge to regarding oneself as merely captive.
shortened: This is sufficient and complete proof that man is ruler over nature and completely overturns the general law of nature. Consider what power, what gift God has given to man that he is ruler over nature, yet man considers himself a prisoner of nature.

order.why: Read the historical comparison of humans and animals in context.
Consider the distinction drawn between compelled movement and will.
Examine the stated response to materialist premises.
shortened: Man possesses certain virtues of which nature is deprived. He exercises volition; nature is without will.

These ideal virtues or powers in man surpass or surround nature, comprehend natural laws and phenomena, penetrate the mysteries of the unknown and invisible and bring them forth into the realm of the known and visible.

order.why: Read the reported argument involving reason, memory and foresight.
shortened: "Nature lacks reason, will power. It cannot discover its own secrets; it cannot foresee the future; it cannot remember the past; it cannot make heavenly discoveries; it cannot communicate with the East and the West in one minute; it cannot imprison the voice in a machine, and so on. This proves that the soul of man is above nature. This sun, with all its light, is a captive, it has no will power, but the spirit of man is above the sun.

order.why: Consider inference about the past and future.
Keep the reported historical example without adopting it as a modern account.
Read the reported examples of lasting effects and transformation.
Consider the scope of environmental alteration in the reported examples.
Read the garden’s need for continued attention.
Distinguish the stated functions of spirit, mind and soul.
shortened: The spirit is the power of life, the mind is the power which apprehendeth the reality of things, and the soul is an intermediary between the Supreme Concourse (or Spiritual World) and the lower concourse (or material world).

order.why: Retain the reported image of spirit governing the body.
shortened: But the Universal Emperor over the entire body is the Spirit. It is the Spirit that rules and controls all the functions of the body...

order.why: Keep the reported philosophical claim concerning mind in nature.
Contrasts nature with the human capacity to discover and direct its powers.
Read the reported healing remark within its full-source distinction of physical remedies.
Consider the claim of an enduring spiritual power.
Read the luminous intellect’s capacity for discovery.
shortened: If the luminous aspect of the human intellect overcometh the world of nature, it will acquire the power of discovery which is the basis for wondrous insights, and become informed about the realities and the characteristics of things.

order.why: Connect developed intellect with training.
Hear the reported appreciation of reason as a gift.
shortened: The Greatest Bestowal of the Lord of mankind to man is this power of reason or intellect. Through it man overcomes all the difficulties; reveals the mysteries of existence, solves the problems of life and attains to the highest station of comprehension….

order.why: Consider the mind as a mirror of realities and spiritual light.
Read effective action as giving material expression to divine will.
shortened: This power gives man effectual control over nature. He is enabled to discover reality and bring invisible things into the courts of the visible. Thus he is enabled to render effective the will of God and give it material station.

order.why: Keep the statement concerning the power of the Kingdom.
shortened: He shall be able to withstand all the forces of the world for he will rise up through the power of the Kingdom and no material power can withstand that mighty force.
The power of God is always victorious over all things.

order.why: Consider the responsibility implied by a high station.
Read willpower in relation to learning and public welfare.
Turn toward attachment to an infinite reality.
shortened: Man must attach himself to an infinite reality so that his glory, his joy and his progress may be infinite. Only the spirit is real; everything else is as shadow.

order.why: Close with the reported pearls of knowledge and virtue that can grow.

questions: Which ordinary invention becomes newly striking when viewed as the discovery of a hidden possibility?
How does the passage about using material laws illuminate the repeated language of breaking nature’s laws?
What assumptions about mind, will, and nature underlie the arguments presented?
How does Bacon’s account of observing causes compare with this collection’s account of discovery?
What responsibilities accompany the ability to alter environments and extend human powers?
How could growth in knowledge and growth in character strengthen—or fail to strengthen—one another?

references.label: 1 · Francis Bacon, Novum Organum I.1–4 · Understanding and power
references.note: The opening aphorisms, in the edition edited by Joseph Devey, connect human power with observation, instruments, and knowledge of causes; nature’s own operations remain essential. Compare this account with both the collection’s language of mastery and its explicit reference to using natural laws. Bacon’s methodological argument is distinct from the passages’ claims about the spiritual reality of the human being.

subjects.displayTitle: Radiance: the fragrance of a life
subjects.introduction: The luminous countenance has no need of ornament. Bahá’u’lláh’s sentence describes a beauty that cannot be bought, and the writings give it a moral texture: justice and praiseworthy character waft the fragrance of purity, a person’s entrance makes a gathering a source of felicitation, and the friends are to be like bright lamps in whatever city they enter, so that strangers conclude from their deeds that such a soul is not of this world. Fragrance and light describe an influence that reaches others before any explanation, the atmosphere a life creates. The images of Joseph’s garment and Jacob’s recovered sight remind us that such perception is also a gift to be received, not a method for judging faces. Matthew’s lamp set on a stand turns attention from the performer toward good works that honour God [1]. Children raised in the holy Teachings, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes, will become sweet airs across the gardens of the world. The road leads on into being a source of light, into joyfulness as the native climate of such a presence, and into the connections of the heart by which one spirit kindles another.
subjects.arc: Begin with unadorned radiance, connect beauty with conduct, and explore how a life brings light to others.

order.why: Consider a presence that blesses each place it enters.
Open with radiance that needs no ornament.
shortened: The adornment of the people of God hath ever been through their own selves and not through outward things. The luminous countenance hath no need of ornament.

order.why: Connect the light of a face with loving-kindness of character.
Ground fragrance in justice and praiseworthy conduct.
shortened: O servant! Conduct thyself with justice and act in such wise that thy deeds may reveal the sanctity of the Cause. Adorn thyself with so praiseworthy a character, that by it the fragrance of purity may be wafted over all men.

order.why: Read sincere and kindly association as a source of sweetness.
shortened: They must mingle with the people of the world with truthfulness, love, sincerity and kindness, creating enthusiasm and rapture, diffusing sweet fragrance and pouring forth refined sugar.

order.why: Hear the reported link between visible conduct and human prosperity.
Consider the candle through sanctity and detachment.
shortened: Today the people of Baha are souls who should become renowned throughout all regions for possessing the character, conduct and behavior of the Supreme Concourse, for He explicitly states in numerous passages that in this wondrous Dispensation a Baha'i is one who, like a candle, illumines and casts the light of sanctity and detachment upon East and West.

order.why: Read the image of souls who are light from head to foot.
shortened: These souls are Baha'i, they are divine, they are luminous, they are of the All-Merciful. They cast no shadow, but are rather light from head to foot.

order.why: Read the garden’s expectation that flowers give fragrance.
shortened: Ye are the flowers of this Garden - it behooveth you that all should perceive from you the fragrance of the All-Merciful. Act ye in a manner befitting this glorious and exalted station.

order.why: Hear the call to embody a nature others can encounter.
shortened: Say: O My loved ones! Be ye of such a nature that the people of creation may inhale from you the sweet fragrances of your Lord, the Most High, the All-Glorious, that your sanctification of His Cause may be made manifest among those who are veiled.

order.why: Read the invitation to appear with divine radiance.
shortened: Appear amongst men with the light of God and His radiance, that from your faces may be witnessed the brightness of your Lord, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate.

order.why: Consider the blessing upon a countenance reflecting the Word.
shortened: Blessed are they from whose countenances radiate the All-Merciful splendor and the lights of the Divine Word.

order.why: Connect beauty with the light of love.
shortened: When the light of the love of God shines upon a face, the countenance attains the utmost grace and beauty.

order.why: Read spiritual beauty as reflected brightness.
shortened: For spiritual beauty and grace are reflected in the brightness of the All-Merciful, and this is evident upon thy brow.

order.why: Hear the image of the Kingdom’s sun.
Consider a personal letter’s recognition of luminous love.
shortened: O illumined candle! You have kindled a countenance of supreme beauty and grace. You are radiant, pleasing, beautiful and majestic, for the light of the love of God shines from your brow like a manifest light.

order.why: Read another letter’s glad acknowledgment.
Connect a response to a portrait with the hope for growing perfections.
Read luminosity as increasing through conduct.
shortened: If thou dost act according to the commandments and exhortations of God, know thou for a certainty that the luminosity of thy face will day by day increase.

order.why: Consider reputation grounded in disposition.
Become a sign of mercy and bounty.
shortened: Be ye signs of His all subduing proof, symbols of His lasting mercy and expressions of His perfect bounty.

order.why: Connect the gardens of hearts with outward light.
shortened: The fragrance of the love of God wafts from the gardens of their hearts to all regions, and the lights of recognition shine forth from their faces through the seven layers of existence.

order.why: Read the human flower through its fragrance.
shortened: O handmaid of God! The rose, hyacinth and thyme require a sweet fragrance and delightful perfume. The sweet-scented fragrance of the human flower is the divine perfume. If this musk-laden scent is diffused from the human flower, that flower will bloom in the garden of all humanity, and that bud will become radiant in the Most Glorious Paradise.

order.why: Consider freshness beside the stream of knowledge.
Hear the prayer to become fruitful land.
Read the growth of saplings into fruitful trees.
Connect children’s education with future influence.
shortened: Among the greatest of all services that can possibly be rendered by man to Almighty God is the education and training of children, young plants of the Abha Paradise, so that these children, fostered by grace in the way of salvation, growing like pearls of divine bounty in the shell of education, will one day bejewel the crown of abiding glory.

I hope that thou wilt acquit thyself well in this most important of tasks, and successfully carry the day, and become an ensign of God's abounding grace; that these children, reared one and all in the holy Teachings, will develop natures like unto the sweet airs that blow across the gardens of the All-Glorious, and will waft their fragrance around the world.

order.why: Read conduct as a means of education and renewal.
Consider the rose-like temperament cultivated in this life.
Describes radiant faces together with detachment, sacrifice and spiritual life.
Bring fragrance into a shared place of remembrance.
shortened: This being the case, care no more for the world and its desires, but cling to the spiritual world and its gifts, spread the fragrances of God, be submissive to the Word of God, establish a spiritual meeting place where from the incense of sanctity and purity will rise up to God, assemble there with fragrance and spirituality and celebrate the Name of your Lord by day and by night.

order.why: Read the feast of fellowship as a place of growing virtue.
shortened: Therefore, this servant is infinitely pleased with them and I hope that day by day they will increase in this virtue, adorn the feast of fellowship, find repose under the shade of His favor, and captivate hearts with the holy fragrances.

order.why: Hear the reported hope for loving conduct in Paris.
Read the reported four qualities, including independent sight and perseverance.
Consider the reported example of cheerfulness amid poverty.
shortened: Although at that time one could hire a donkey for five cents, yet he could not very well afford this lavish expenditure. Nevertheless you never saw him cross or sour-tempered. He was a source of delight and happiness to all. Such souls are the bright gems in the crown of existence.... They belong to another world, they are living in the highest spiritual altitude, they are permeated through and through with the quintessence of renunciation.

order.why: Hear the reported lasting effect of a brief encounter.
shortened: There are some souls whose spiritual constitutions are so etherealized that although they live in this world yet they belong to another realm. They breath another air, they speak another language and walk on another plane. If one associate and converse with them for one moment, he will never forget them.

order.why: Read the reported reflections of humanitarian purpose.
Consider the reported welcome of a meeting imagined as a garden.
shortened: That the faces of the Believers shall be like sunshine, like the open rose, so that every one entering the meeting will recognize the light which they possess. It will be like a man entering a garden, and though he may have a cold and so be unable to inhale the perfume, yet he can see the full beauty and the freshness of the flowers.

order.why: Retain the memorial’s recollection of a luminous face.
shortened: He was a man amazing to behold, his face so luminous that even those who were not believers used to say that a heavenly light shone from his forehead.

order.why: Read countenance as a sign within the Book of Certitude’s interpretive setting.
Consider the scriptural image of the brightness of bliss.
Keep the counsel concerning a receptive encounter.
Read the relationship between radiance and perception of fragrance.
shortened: That which is attributed to the Truth is indeed musk whose fragrance is diffused, yet none can detect it save those who turn to the All-Merciful with radiant countenance.

order.why: Introduce Jacob’s perception of Joseph’s garment.
Read the garment’s fragrance with the recovery of sight.
Hear the invitation to sew a fragrant shirt.
Consider the recognition of love through its effects.
shortened: The love of the Abha Beauty perfumes the nostrils like musk and ambergris - it cannot be mistaken. Consider what a sweet fragrance you perceived from those divine friends. Can such holy fragrances be perceived from other directions? No, by God! The matter is evident and manifest, and the truth is clear and present.

order.why: Acknowledge someone who enabled another to perceive the fragrance.
Read the effort needed to share glad tidings.
shortened: Now, too, receptivity in that land is great, but a mighty effort is needed if the friends are to impart these joyful tidings with gladness and delight, and to perfume the senses of the seekers with the fragrance of the robe of the divine Joseph.

order.why: Connect steadfastness with becoming a herald.
shortened: O thou who art perfumed by the breaths of God's love!

I have read thy letter and have supplicated unto God that He may accept thee into His Kingdom, make thee worthy to be called a child of the Kingdom, and render thee firm as mighty mountains in God's Covenant, and a herald of His Great Covenant which He hath established through a trace of His Supreme Pen with the dwellers of the heavens and earth, until thou mayest be confirmed to diffuse the fragrance of holiness throughout those regions and climes.

order.why: Hear the reported hope for enduring service as a channel.
Read the reported call to be alive with fragrance.
Hear the brief reported image of flowers giving scent.
shortened: They are the flowers of the garden of ABHA--they must breathe forth their fragrance!..

order.why: Keep the distinctive devotional image of a torch guiding through darkness.
shortened: I testify that by the torch of your body, blazing in the pitch darkness, you revealed the paths through the gloom until you guided Khidr to the darknesses.

order.why: Close with the reported wish for loved ones to shine like a star.

questions: What qualities make a person’s presence feel welcoming or life-giving?
How do the images of light and fragrance convey different kinds of influence?
What keeps the aspiration to radiance from becoming concern with appearances or a judgment of another person’s face?
How do the passages connect joy with justice, kindness, and perseverance?
What does Matthew’s direction beyond the performer add to the idea of visible good works?
How might a gathering cultivate an atmosphere in which people feel both welcomed and encouraged to grow?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 5:14–16 · A lamp that gives light
references.note: The lamp illuminates the household, and visible good works direct praise toward the Father. Compare this outward benefit with the compilation’s images of fragrance and radiance. The connection concerns conduct that helps others perceive spiritual qualities, rather than a demand to attract admiration or display a particular physical appearance.

subjects.displayTitle: Recompense: the fruit of a life
subjects.introduction: The reward of a lamp, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once remarked, is its own illumination; it asks for no other payment. Recompense in the Bahá’í writings begins with that quiet thought and then opens outward, for Bahá’u’lláh also insists that no act performed goes without its fruit, that a single breath drawn for God leaves its trace in creation, and that each of us will one day be asked what our hands have wrought. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishes two kinds of reward: the perfections a soul gains while still in this world, which are themselves a paradise, and the gifts that await it after its ascension. Between those poles lie the Báb’s image of wasted deeds as a mirage and letters of consolation to the bereaved and to the fathers of martyrs, assuring them that nothing endured for God is lost. Jesus’ warning against charity performed for an audience raises the same question of whose notice we are really seeking [1]. The subject leads on to heaven and paradise, to the pairing of reward and punishment, and to the confirmations promised to those who teach.
subjects.arc: Begin with a deed’s inherent value, explore consequence and spiritual reward, and return to gratitude and sincere service.

order.why: Open with the reported lamp whose light is its reward.
shortened: "The greatest reward for a man is to see his life well-spent and useful. The reward of the lamp is its own illumination. It does not require any other compensation. Good deeds are their own rewards." he said.

order.why: Read inherent reward beside the claim that deeds bear fruit.
shortened: Likewise apprehend thou the nature of hell-fire and be of them that truly believe. For every act performed there shall be a recompense according to the estimate of God, and unto this the very ordinances and prohibitions prescribed by the Almighty amply bear witness. For surely if deeds were not rewarded and yielded no fruit, then the Cause of God - exalted is He - would prove futile. Immeasurably high is He exalted above such blasphemies! However, unto them that are rid of all attachments a deed is, verily, its own reward.

order.why: Consider virtues themselves as spiritual reward.
shortened: Again, another spirit may be perfect, wise, knowing, possessed of praiseworthy virtues and human perfections. These virtues are in themselves the reward of this spirit.

order.why: Distinguish present perfections from ultimate rewards.
shortened: For rewards and punishments are said to be of two kinds, one being existential rewards and punishments and the other, ultimate rewards and punishments. Existential paradise and hell are to be found in all the worlds of God, whether in this world or in the heavenly realms of the spirit, and to gain these rewards is to attain life eternal.

The ultimate rewards are the gifts and perfections that man attains in the spiritual realms after his ascension from this world, while the existential rewards are those true and luminous perfections which are attained while still abiding in this world and which are the cause of everlasting life.

order.why: Hear the assurance that no sincere effort is lost.
shortened: The reward of no soul hath been lost, nor shall it be lost. If anyone draweth a single breath for the sake of God, its effects shall assuredly appear in creation. Verily thy Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read the concrete example of respectfully carrying a casket.
shortened: Now that you have arisen to perform this righteous deed and carried that deceased one's casket with the utmost respect, causing others to marvel, rest assured that the recompense for these good deeds will be bestowed from the Kingdom of the Lord of Signs.

order.why: Consider remembered kindness to prisoners.
shortened: This is why I sent a message to Mirza 'Ali-Asghar Aminu's-Sultan that one night, regarding his consideration toward the captives of God - Jinab-i-Mulla 'Ali-Akbar, Jinab-i-Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, Jinab-i-Amin, Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah - those who were imprisoned in Tehran, when it was mentioned in the Most Holy Court, He said: "If someone is going, take him this message, or write to him, that this consideration he showed toward these prisoners will not be forgotten in the divine Kingdom, therefore let him be assured that he will see its recompense."

order.why: Keep the reported reward of the truthful spy in its story setting.
Connect service, lasting effects and release from petty expectation.
shortened: Service to the Cause of God consists of detachment and sanctification, abstraction and unity, and the manifestation of merciful attributes among humanity. The fruit and effect of this service is ancient glory for humanity in all divine worlds.

Even at the point of dust, which is the lowest and basest of stations, observe how even in the world of dust and mineral the traces of certain souls are extant and evident. Draw thy lesson from this and take warning.
How long shall we remain captive in this snare for the sake of a grain, and stay imprisoned and sorrowful in this cage hoping for a mere morsel?

order.why: Read the harvest of conduct in the heavenly realm.
Consider the reported consequences of misconduct.
Read the summons to account for one’s actions.
shortened: Say: O people, the world and all that is therein shall pass away, and you shall return to the holy presence before God, the True King, the Manifest One, and shall be questioned concerning what you did in your vain life, and shall be recompensed for what your hands have wrought.

order.why: Hear the declaration of the Day of requital.
Keep the contrast between heedlessness and rewarded effort.
shortened: Soon shall the heedless behold the recompense of their deeds, and you shall witness your reward with God, the Most High, the Great.

order.why: Consider the disclosure of one’s deeds after death.
shortened: As for the spirits of the infidels, by My life, at the time of death they recognize what has passed them by, and they lament and implore. Likewise after their spirits depart from their bodies. It is very clear and evident that after death all will become aware of their deeds and actions. By the Sun of the horizon of might! The people of truth will at that time experience such joy as cannot be described. Similarly, the people of error will be seized by such fear, anxiety and terror as cannot be imagined.

order.why: Read the reported analogy of capacities understood in a new world.
shortened: As to the child who was blind and deaf in the womb, until he reaches this world, he does not realize his own imperfections. So with those who refuse the Truth here--they will realize how imperfect they are only when they attain the next world where the use of belief is employed. It is known that when we pass from this world to the other, that every good thing or delight or every bad thing will be the result of actions here.

order.why: Hear the warning of remorse for injustice to oneself.
Keep the lament concerning neglected opportunities.
Consider the contrast between lasting light and regret.
shortened: This one becomes the eternal culture and melody of the everlasting world, while that one's end is regret in this world without name or fame. That one is eternal light, and this one everlasting remorse.

order.why: Read the Báb’s imagery of deeds as mirage and fire.
shortened: Soon will God show them their deeds as sources of regret unto themselves, scattered dust upon the earth, like a mirage in the desert which the thirsty one supposeth to be water, until, when he cometh unto it, he findeth it to be nothing, and they shall find their deeds in hell as fire upon fire intensified.
This is the recompense for having been wretched regarding Our true verses contrary to the truth.

order.why: Hold the fruits of knowledge beside the imagery of Zaqqum.
Consider the force of the statement concerning recognition.
shortened: And if in this Day one should forsake all deeds but attain unto recognition of the Truth, there remaineth for him hope of salvation; but should he, God forbid, be veiled from the Truth while occupied with all manner of deeds, there is no escape for him and he shall be reckoned by God among the people of hell, negation and fire.

order.why: Read recognition of the Day in relation to paradise.
shortened: Verily, he who hath attained unto this Day is reckoned among the denizens of Paradise in the sight of God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Hear the blessing for turning and believing.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath inhaled the fragrance of the All-Merciful and hath beheld His noble countenance. Blessed art thou for having turned towards the Most Sublime Horizon and believed in God, the Mighty, the Great.

order.why: Connect remembrance with a goodly end.
shortened: Whoso hath attained unto the remembrance of God in His days, he is of those who have attained unto all good and for whom there is a goodly end.

order.why: Read remembrance as grace for those who trust.
shortened: As to those who believe in thee in the Book, We shall assuredly remember them as a grace from Us, that they may be mindful. Those who hasten to the mercy of their Lord - these are the sincere ones. And those who place their trust in Him in any matter - these are they that trust. Glory be unto them, before and after, though they know it not.

order.why: Hear the promise of recompense for deeds.
shortened: Verily God will reward them with the best of what they have wrought in this earthly life, and verily there is no God but He, the Strong, the Mighty.

order.why: Read the promise concerning commandments and gardens of eternity.
Consider the image of a beautiful form at resurrection.
Keep the Báb’s distinctive imagery of the life to come.
Explains the promised reward for belief and good deeds across religious communities.
Retain the reported description of paradises and estrangement.
shortened: And in the next world too, there are countless paradises prepared for the believers and sincere ones, and the spirits of holy souls enjoy all heavenly blessings and divine favors, while the spirits of the deniers and people of error and the adversaries are caught in hell and torment, abased and humiliated.

order.why: Read the reported statement concerning deserved punishment.
shortened: Our Lord said: By the Justice and judgment of God those who commit evil suffer and are punished for it and eternal punishment is merited by these evil-doers.

order.why: Place beside it the reported account of progress from suffering.
shortened: Evil man will be in a state of torture out of which they must progress. The good man progress out of it in the flesh because of the torture they suffered while in the life here.

order.why: Consider the reported educational purpose of divine judgment.
shortened: God judges not as we judge; He looks at the intentions of the heart. Also His punishment is always to cure, to redeem, to educate, so that we may become radiant sons of God."

order.why: Read the particular argument against a second penalty.
Consider contrasting fruits of suffering and harmful conduct.
shortened: The suffering soul will attain great benefit whereas the other will fall into manifest loss. This one will pluck the fruit of salvation from the tree of life whereas the other will obtain the bitter zaqun from the orchard of his hopes. This field will see divine blessings. That earth will cause the shrub of hopelessness to grow.

order.why: Hear consolation for one who has borne tribulations.
Read the transformation of bitter cups into sweetness.
shortened: Soon all these pains and trials shall be compensated in the Kingdom of Holiness that transcends the comprehension of souls. Each arrow shall have the effect of a hundred thousand favors of the Luminous Beauty, and each bitter cup shall yield a hundred thousand seas of matchless sweetness. Soon shall ye behold the fruits of these tribulations in the Most Glorious Kingdom.

order.why: Receive the assurance addressed to one who endured hardship.
Keep the consolation addressed to a father of martyred sons.
shortened: All will pass away and vanish to nothingness but the son who hath been offered up by his father and the father who hath sacrificed his son shall both shine like the twin Pleiades in the firmament of everlasting glory and shall be seated on the starry throne of everlasting sovereignty.
Great is their blessedness! All happiness be theirs and all bounty, through the light of this favour that has illumined both earth and heaven with grace.

order.why: Read the prayer for sorrow to yield illumination and steadfastness.
Consider the promise of lasting glory beyond worldly rank.
shortened: But praise be to God, you were assisted to a life whose end is joy and success, and eternal glory in the divine realm.
All kings will envy your station and covet your glory, for you have placed upon your head the crown of the Most Great Guidance whose brilliant jewels cast their rays across centuries and ages.

order.why: Hear the particular assurance concerning hopes fulfilled.
shortened: Then you will witness eternal sovereignty and the crown of everlasting dominion. All hopes and desires, whether in this world or the next, will be fulfilled and all aims will be achieved.

order.why: Read the expansive numerical image of generosity.
shortened: If in the previous Dispensation it was revealed "Whoso performeth a good deed shall receive a tenfold reward," praise be to God, in this mightiest Dispensation a hundredthousandfold reward is ordained and established.

order.why: Keep the Báb’s distinctive promise concerning blessing and visitation.
Hear the glad tidings offered to the steadfast.
Contrast the passing world with enduring divine bounty.
shortened: The world and all that is therein shall perish; then shall the sincere ones find that which hath been ordained for them in the Most Great Paradise from God, the Forgiving, the Generous.

order.why: Consider the assurance of peace and bliss.
shortened: I swear by My life! The true believer, after his ascension, shall find himself in a state of eternal peace and everlasting bliss.

order.why: Read refuge and paradise in the language of praise.
shortened: Praised be to He Who hath given refuge to the sincere ones in His All-highest bounty! Praised be to He Who hath brought the believers in the Unity of God into the paradise of His dwelling place!

order.why: Hear the prayer linking service, family and fitting reward.
Turn from receiving bounty toward gratitude.
shortened: These favors have We bestowed upon thee as a bounty on Our part and a mercy from Our presence, that thou mayest be of those who are grateful.

order.why: Close with the invitation to continual thanksgiving.
shortened: Offer a hundred thousand thanksgivings at every moment that you have become the recipient of such favors and the manifestation of such bounties.

questions: What might it mean for a good deed to be its own reward while also bearing future fruit?
How do the distinctions between present and ultimate rewards change your reading of paradise?
What motives emerge when an action receives little recognition or seems unsuccessful?
How should letters of consolation be read with attention to the people and losses they address?
What does Matthew’s contrast between public approval and hidden devotion add to these passages?
How could hope in the lasting value of action encourage care without becoming calculation about reward?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 6:1–6 · The reward of hidden devotion
references.note: Jesus contrasts charity and prayer performed for an audience with acts directed toward the Father who sees in secret. Compare the question of motive with the compilation’s statement that a deed can be its own reward. Matthew retains the language of divine recompense; the comparison invites reflection on different kinds of recognition rather than the elimination of all hope of reward.
